profile.about: IIIT Allahabad is a centrally funded IIIT set up in 1999 and declared an Institute of National Importance under the IIIT Act in 2014. It is a compact, fully residential campus of about 100 acres at Jhalwa on the edge of Prayagraj, laid out on a Penrose-geometry plan, with four departments: Information Technology, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Applied Sciences and Management Studies. Undergraduate intake is concentrated in three B.Tech streams (IT, ECE and IT with Business Informatics) plus five-year dual degrees, and the institute has held a NIRF Engineering rank in the 87-103 range in recent years. Its strengths lie in computing research areas such as AI, robotics, computer vision, cryptography and bioinformatics, run through dedicated centres alongside the departments.

curriculumHighlights.text: IIITA's B.Tech Ordinance-2023 (NEP-aligned, effective AY 2023-24) sets a 160-credit, 8-semester degree that pairs a core Major with a mandatory 15-credit multidisciplinary Minor; a Double Major option is planned for a future rollout.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program with NEP Aligned Curriculum - Sections 3(d)-(f), 4.0-4.11 (160 credits, Major + Mandatory Minor)

curriculumHighlights.text: An optional B.Tech Honours needs 15 extra credits in the student's own branch, a minimum 8.0 CGPI with no backlog, an academic 8th-semester project, and at least one Tier-I/II or SCI publication (or a filed patent).

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Section 5(g) Honors eligibility

curriculumHighlights.text: NEP-style multiple exits let a student leave with a UG Certificate after year 1 (40 credits), a UG Diploma after year 2 (80 credits), or a B.Sc.(Engineering) after year 3 (120 credits), each needing a few additional prescribed credits.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Section 4.21 Honorable Exit Options

curriculumHighlights.text: Grading is a 60:40 continuous-assessment split: a 35-mark formative Part-1 (quizzes/assignments/labs), a 25-mark mid-semester exam, and a 40-mark end-semester exam, converted to a relative A+-to-F letter grade on a 10-point scale.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Sections 5 and 14.0 Marks Distribution and Grading System

curriculumHighlights.text: 75% attendance is compulsory in every course or the student is deregistered from it; a student may register for at most 28 credits (backlog plus current courses) in a semester.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Sections 9 and 14.6 Attendance Requirements

curriculumHighlights.text: A one-time branch change is allowed at the end of semester 1, open only to students who cleared every first-semester course with an SGPI of 7.50 or above; it depends on seats in the target branch and ignores category/reservation.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Section 17 Branch Change

curriculumHighlights.text: Up to 40% of credits in a course type may come from NPTEL/SWAYAM online courses (up to 5% as self-study credit); the normal 4-year degree can extend via spill-over semesters 9-12, up to 6 years for General/OBC and 7 years for SC/ST/PwD students.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Sections 6(l), 8 and 5(j) online courses, duration, spill-over semesters

curriculumHighlights.text: A CGPI of 8.50 or above earns the B.Tech degree 'with Distinction'; only students who finish all 160 credits within the first 8 successive semesters remain eligible for institute ranks, medals and merit-based fellowships.

sources.title: IIIT-A: The Ordinance-2023 for B.Tech Program - Section 5(h) Distinction and 5(j) Ranks/Medals

research.note: Research runs through five institute centres alongside the four departments: the Center for Cognitive Computing, the Center for Intelligent Robotics, the Rekhi Center for Science of Happiness, the Center for Continuing Education and Outreach Program, and a NewGen IEDC innovation cell. Each department runs its own Ph.D. programme (IT; ECE; Applied Sciences, spanning Bioinformatics, Biomedical Engineering, Mathematics, Physics and Statistics; and Management Studies), and IT also offers a combined M.Tech-Ph.D. track. IIITA's own pages do not publish a current headcount of enrolled scholars.

summary.text: Student activity at IIIT Allahabad runs through the Gymkhana and about eight official clubs spanning literary, sports, drama, music, technical and audio-visual interests, alongside the separate technical society GeekHaven and the robotics club Robita. The year builds toward two flagship fests: Effervescence, a multi-day cultural gathering in October, and Aparoksha, the technical fest in April, with the sports meet Asmita rounding out the calendar. Sports infrastructure centres on a football ground with an athletics track, a swimming pool, and courts for basketball, tennis, squash and volleyball, plus indoor games at the Student Activity Centre.

items.q: What is IIIT Allahabad, and when was it set up?
items.a: IIIT Allahabad is a public technical institute in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, built around information technology and its allied fields. It started in 1999 as a centre of excellence in IT, was given deemed-university status in 2000, and Parliament's IIIT Act made it an Institute of National Importance from 1 December 2014, putting it on the same statutory footing as the other MHRD-funded IIITs.

sources.title: IIIT Allahabad home page
Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad

items.q: How do I get admission into the B.Tech program at IIIT Allahabad?
items.a: There is no separate institute-level entrance test for the B.Tech programmes. Seats are filled through JEE (Main) rank via JoSAA's central counselling, the same process used for NITs and other IIITs, and any seats left after the JoSAA rounds are offered through the CSAB special round.

sources.title: Institute Profile - IIIT Allahabad (Institute Code 309)

items.q: Which B.Tech branches does IIIT Allahabad offer, and how big is each one?
items.a: The four-year B.Tech is offered in three branches: Electronics & Communication Engineering (121 seats), Information Technology (242 seats) and Information Technology-Business Informatics (40 seats), per the JoSAA seat matrix. These are the branch names and seat counts JoSAA allots against for this institute; actual availability can shift a little year to year as the authority updates the matrix.

sources.title: Institute Profile - IIIT Allahabad (Institute Code 309)

items.q: Does IIIT Allahabad offer a 5-year integrated degree?
items.a: Yes. Besides the standalone four-year B.Tech branches, JoSAA also allots seats to three five-year dual-degree tracks run by the institute: B.Tech + M.Tech in Electronics & Communication Engineering (11 seats), B.Tech + M.Tech in Information Technology (25 seats), and B.Tech (IT-Business Informatics) + MBA (22 seats). A student who wants the extra postgraduate credential without a separate admission cycle applies to one of these tracks directly through JoSAA rather than converting later.

sources.title: Institute Profile - IIIT Allahabad (Institute Code 309)

items.q: Where exactly is the IIIT Allahabad campus?
items.a: The campus sits at Devghat, Jhalwa, in Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh, PIN 211015 - a locality on the western side of the city, away from the older University of Allahabad campus. The institute's own contact page lists this address and a Prayagraj landline for enquiries, and all official correspondence uses this location.

sources.title: IIIT Allahabad home page

items.q: What are the hostel arrangements like for students?
items.a: There are eight hostels in all: five for men (BH-1 to BH-5) and three for women (GH-1 to GH-3), run by the institute's Council of Wardens. Freshers usually start in triple-sharing rooms and move to double or single rooms as they move up the years, subject to availability. Every hostel has a centralised mess serving breakfast, lunch, evening snacks and dinner on a fixed daily schedule, along with round-the-clock caretaker support, Wi-Fi, a common recreation area and laundry facilities.

sources.title: Hostels & Living - Council of Wardens

items.q: How are M.Tech admissions conducted at IIIT Allahabad?
items.a: Most M.Tech programmes admit through CCMT (Centralized Counselling for M.Tech/M.Arch/M.Plan) and require a valid GATE score; the discipline of the candidate's GATE paper does not have to match the M.Tech specialisation applied for. Sponsored candidates and NRI/foreign nationals are screened differently - through work experience plus a qualifying degree, or GRE scores, instead of GATE. A few specialised programmes run their own process: the M.Tech in Data Science and Analytics, for instance, sets no minimum GATE score at all and instead selects candidates through its own two-hour, 100-mark online admission test followed by an interview.

sources.title: Admissions - Human Computer Interaction, IIIT Allahabad
Frequently Asked Questions - M.Tech in Data Science and Analytics

items.q: What does it take to get into a PhD program at IIIT Allahabad?
items.a: The regular PhD route needs a qualifying score in GATE, NET-JRF, CSIR-NET, CAT or a similar national exam (M.Tech-holders are exempt from GATE), together with at least 60% marks or a 6.0 CGPA at the postgraduate level - or 70%/7.0 CGPA for direct entry straight after a four-year undergraduate degree. Candidates who did their qualifying degree abroad can offer GRE or GMAT scores instead. Separately, the institute runs a Working Professionals PhD track that waives the qualifying-exam requirement altogether for candidates already employed in relevant industry or academic roles.

items.q: How have IIIT Allahabad's placements been doing recently?
items.a: In the institute's own 2026 placement statistics, 535 of 615 students who registered across UG and PG programmes were placed, an overall rate of about 87%. Looking at B.Tech alone, 433 of 470 registrants were placed (about 92%), with an average CTC of Rs 33.35 lakh per annum and a highest offer of Rs 150 LPA. For the M.Tech/MBA cohort, 102 of 145 registrants were placed (about 70%), averaging Rs 18.24 LPA with a top offer of Rs 47 LPA.

sources.title: Placement Statistics

items.q: Does IIIT Allahabad have specialised research centres beyond its regular departments?
items.a: Yes. Alongside its four core academic departments - Information Technology, Electronics & Communication Engineering, Applied Sciences and Management Studies - the institute runs a set of dedicated research centres, including the Rekhi Centre for Science of Happiness, the Centre for Intelligent Robotics and the Centre for Cognitive Computing, that host cross-department research outside the standard degree structure.

profile.about: IIT Bombay is the second IIT, set up in Powai, Mumbai in 1958 with UNESCO and Soviet assistance and made an institution of national importance by Parliament in 1961. It runs 17 departments, 10 academic centres and 3 schools, has roughly 13,000 students and close to 800 regular faculty, and admits about 1,400 undergraduates a year through JEE (Advanced). It has placed third in NIRF overall and engineering in the last two editions and is among the top Indian institutions in the QS World University Rankings, with particular depth in computing, electrical engineering and sponsored research.

items.q: How do I get into IIT Bombay's B.Tech, Dual Degree, B.S. or B.Des programmes?
items.a: B.Tech, the 5-year Dual Degree and the B.S. programmes take students only through JEE (Advanced) followed by JoSAA seat allocation. B.Des at the IDC School of Design is filled through UCEED. A small number of B.S. (Mathematics) seats go to students who qualify the Indian National Mathematical Olympiad (INMO). There is no separate institute-level entrance test for these programmes.

sources.title: Bachelors Admissions - Academic Office, IIT Bombay

items.q: Which B.Tech branches does IIT Bombay offer through JoSAA, and how many seats are there?
items.a: For 2025-26 the institute sanctioned 1,006 B.Tech seats across 11 branches: Aerospace (66), Chemical (113), Civil (130), Computer Science (170), Electrical (90), Energy Science (41), Engineering Physics (52), Environmental Science (37), Industrial Engineering & OR (36), Mechanical (169) and Metallurgical Engineering & Materials Science (102). Female supernumerary seats are added on top to reach 20% women enrolment, and PwBD reservation is 5% horizontal.

sources.title: Sanctioned Strength for B.Tech for the Academic Year 2025-26
Bachelors Admissions - Academic Office, IIT Bombay

items.q: Can I change my branch after the first year at IIT Bombay?
items.a: No, not into another JoSAA branch. The Senate (256th meeting) removed branch change into JoSAA-administered branches for students admitted through JEE (Advanced) 2023 onwards. The only remaining route is conversion into the Liberal Arts, Sciences and Engineering (LASE) B.S. programme after the first two semesters, which needs an eligibility CPI of at least 7.0 in specified first-year courses plus a test and/or interview. The branch you get through JoSAA is the branch you graduate in.

sources.title: Rules & Regulations for Undergraduate Programmes (Updated August 2026), Section 8 Change of Branch

items.q: Can a B.Tech student convert to a Dual Degree (B.Tech + M.Tech) at IIT Bombay?
items.a: Yes. A B.Tech, B.S. or B.Des student may apply to convert to the 5-year Dual Degree in the same department after the 6th semester and up to a week before the 7th semester starts. Each department's DUGC sets its own conditions, typically a CPI cut-off, a plan for the extra courses and a faculty recommendation. There is also an Interdisciplinary Dual Degree (IDDDP) into another department, open at the end of the 6th semester to students with CPI of 7.5 or more and no FR/DR/DX grades.

sources.title: Rules & Regulations for Undergraduate Programmes (Updated August 2026), Sections 13-14

items.q: What are Minors and Honours at IIT Bombay, and can a CSE Minor substitute for a branch change?
items.a: A Minor is 30 extra credits of courses in a discipline other than your own; every academic unit offers one and the degree reads 'B.Tech in X with Minor in Y'. Honours is 24 extra credits of advanced courses in your own department. Minor course seats are allotted by CPI after pre-registration, so popular minors are competitive. A Minor gives you a credential on the degree certificate and transcript, but it does not change your major.

sources.title: Rules & Regulations for Undergraduate Programmes (Updated August 2026), Section 2.5 Minor and Honours

items.q: How much are the academic fees for a new B.Tech entrant at IIT Bombay?
items.a: For Autumn Semester 2026-27 the tuition fee is Rs 1,00,000 per semester for Indian nationals. With registration/examination, gymkhana, benevolent fund, insurance and medical fees, the per-semester academic total is Rs 1,08,150. The first semester adds one-time charges of Rs 16,000 (admission, alumni life membership, welfare fund) and refundable deposits of Rs 10,000, making the first bill Rs 1,34,150. Hostel and mess charges are billed separately by the Hostel Coordinating Unit.

items.q: Is there a tuition fee waiver at IIT Bombay for SC/ST/PwD students or low-income families?
items.a: Yes. SC, ST and PwD students pay no tuition fee at all. For other UG students, family gross income below Rs 1 lakh a year gives full tuition remission and income between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5 lakh gives two-thirds remission; a parental income certificate must be submitted with the application every year. SC/ST students with family income up to Rs 5 lakh can also get free basic messing, hostel room-rent exemption and a pocket allowance of Rs 500 a month for 10 months.

items.q: What is the Merit-cum-Means (MCM) scholarship at IIT Bombay?
items.a: MCM is the institute's own scholarship for at most 25% of the sanctioned UG intake, open to students with family income up to Rs 5 lakh a year. It waives tuition and pays Rs 40,000 a year (income up to Rs 1 lakh), Rs 30,000 (Rs 1-3 lakh) or Rs 20,000 (Rs 3-5 lakh); women students get a further Rs 10,000 Women Merit Scholarship. First-year merit is the JEE (Advanced) rank (UCEED for B.Des); later years use academic performance. It cannot be clubbed with other scholarships.

items.q: How does hostel allotment work for first-year students at IIT Bombay?
items.a: Every UG entrant gets a hostel room; the campus has 21 residence halls run by the Hostel Coordinating Unit with the student Hostel Affairs Council. For the 2026 batch the room number came in the welcome email around 17 July, check-in opened on 20 July at a common registration desk near Hostel 1, and orientation ran 21-25 July before classes on 27 July. Parents are not allowed inside hostels. A Semester Mess Advance is paid on the ASC portal beforehand; hostel fees follow a separate HCU circular.

items.q: Where is IIT Bombay and how do I reach the campus from the station or airport?
items.a: The campus is in Powai, north-east Mumbai (PIN 400076), between Powai and Vihar lakes. On the Central suburban line, Kanjurmarg (about 3 km) and Vikhroli are the closest stations; on the Western line, Andheri is about 10 km away. Saki Naka on Metro Line 1 is roughly 4 km from campus and Aarey JVLR on the Aqua Line also works; take an auto-rickshaw from either. BEST buses stop at IIT Main Gate and IIT Market Gate. From the international airport it is a short taxi or metro-plus-auto ride.

sources.title: Contact Us / How to Reach - IIT Bombay

items.q: What is the medium of instruction and grading system at IIT Bombay?
items.a: All teaching and examinations are in English. Performance is reported as a CPI on a 10-point scale; the institute awards no class or division and states that the CPI cannot simply be converted to a percentage by a fixed factor, though notionally CPI x 10 is used where a percentage is demanded. B.Tech, B.S. and B.Des are 4-year (8-semester) programmes and the Dual Degree is 5 years (10 semesters).

items.q: What do IIT Bombay's placement numbers look like for B.Tech graduates?
items.a: In the institute's NIRF 2025 submission, 990 students of the 4-year UG programmes graduated on time in 2023-24; 731 were placed at a median salary of Rs 19.61 lakh per annum and 259 went on to higher studies. For the 5-year programmes, 156 of 182 graduates were placed at a median of Rs 19.25 lakh. Campus placements are run by the student-managed Placement Office through the portal at campus.placements.iitb.ac.in; the institute has not published a public branch-wise CPI cut-off for registration.

items.q: If I withdraw after paying fees at IIT Bombay, how much do I get back?
items.a: If you withdraw before the last date for paying the semester fee, the semester fee is refunded after deducting Rs 5,000 as seat-acceptance fee and processing charges. If you withdraw after that date, only the refundable caution deposits (institute, library and hostel) are returned, subject to no-dues, and mess charges are collected pro-rata for the days used.

sources.title: Schedule for Payment of Academic Fees by UG New Entrants, Autumn Semester 2026-27 (Fee Refund Policy)

items.q: Can I finish B.Tech early or leave with an exit degree at IIT Bombay?
items.a: B.Tech and B.S. students who complete all credit requirements can apply to leave at the end of a semester after at least three years in the institute; the degree is still conferred at the batch's regular convocation and recorded as a 4-year programme. Such students may register for placements but get no hostel accommodation during placement activities. The rulebook also provides an exit-degree option for undergraduates and an early-exit route for Dual Degree students.

sources.title: Rules & Regulations for Undergraduate Programmes (Updated August 2026), Sections 9.4-9.5 and 12

items.q: What should I do before arriving at IIT Bombay as a fresher?
items.a: Before reporting, set up your institute IT account via the Computer Centre page, fill personal details on the ASC portal, pay the Semester Mess Advance, and print the pre-filled Student/Parent Declaration, Hostel Registration and Medical Record forms. Carry your JoSAA/UCEED/INMO allotment letter, originals plus copies of certificates, and immunisation records (MMR, chickenpox, typhoid, hepatitis A recommended). The Gymkhana's Student Mentor Programme and NewBee portal help freshers settle in.

profile.about: IIT Madras was set up in 1959 under an Indo-German agreement, declared an Institute of National Importance in 1961 and later named an Institute of Eminence. It has held the top spot in NIRF's engineering ranking every year since the framework began and the overall ranking for seven straight years. Eighteen departments span engineering, sciences, humanities, management and medical science, and doctoral scholars outnumber undergraduates on a wooded campus that also houses the IITM Research Park and incubation cell.

curriculumHighlights.text: Branch change happens once, at the end of the first semester, on first-semester performance alone. A branch may lose or gain at most 10% of its strength, at least one student per discipline is always considered, and Engineering Design dual-degree students are excluded.

curriculumHighlights.text: B.Tech (Honours) is opted into during the fourth semester by students with CGPA 8.5 or above after the third semester and every course cleared at first attempt; it needs at least 12 extra professional-major credits plus a compulsory project.

sources.title: Ordinances and Regulations: B.Tech / B.Tech (Honours), IIT Madras (R.1.12 and R.2.8)

curriculumHighlights.text: Minor streams start in the fifth semester: a package of at least three courses coordinated by one department (others may participate), so a student can add a second discipline alongside the professional major.

curriculumHighlights.text: A 4-year B.Tech can convert to the 5-year B.Tech + M.Tech dual degree within the same department during the sixth semester, provided CGPA is at least 8.0 after the fifth semester and there are no backlogs; dual-degree students cannot move back to the 4-year track.

curriculumHighlights.text: Interdisciplinary Dual Degrees (IDDD) let a B.Tech student of any branch with CGPA 8.0 or more after the fifth semester add an M.Tech from the sixth semester in areas such as Quantum Science and Technology, Advanced Materials, Complex Systems or Quantitative Finance; 12 IDDDs existed by December 2022.

curriculumHighlights.text: Semester exchange through the Office of Global Engagement: apply after three to four semesters with no backlogs and preferably a CGPA of 7.5 or more, spend five to six months at a partner university, and budget roughly Rs 4-6 lakh depending on the country.

curriculumHighlights.text: Credit-based curriculum with elective baskets: B.Tech and dual-degree students may earn up to 36 credits through NPTEL or approved online courses (never for core courses), and from the fifth semester a CGPA-linked cap limits how many credits can be registered per semester.

summary.text: Student life at IIT Madras is organised around 20 river-named hostels that compete all year in inter-hostel literary, technical and sports leagues. The student-run Centre for Innovation houses a dozen tinkering clubs and competition teams, the Sangam umbrella runs the cultural and literary clubs, and January brings back-to-back flagship fests: Shaastra (technical) and Saarang (cultural). The wooded 617-acre campus, shared with deer and blackbuck, adds a very different backdrop to an engineering degree.

items.q: Can I change my branch after the first year at IIT Madras?
items.a: Branch change is considered only once, at the end of the first semester, purely on first-semester performance. Everyone who clears the first-semester courses is eligible except Engineering Design dual-degree students, subject to vacancies: a branch may not shrink or grow by more than 10% of its strength, though at least one student per discipline is always considered. Dual-degree students cannot switch to a 4-year B.Tech, and the Senate may revise these rules (Regs R.5.1-R.5.8).

sources.title: B.Tech / B.Tech (Honours) Ordinances and Regulations (2015 batch onwards), R.5.0 Change of Branch

items.q: Which hostel do first-year B.Tech students get, and are rooms shared?
items.a: For the 2026 batch, first-year boys are housed in Mandakini-B (5th to 9th floors) and first-year girls in Swarnamukhi; only shared rooms are given to freshers. Senior students get single, double or triple rooms depending on the hostel. Room allotment happens at the hostel office on the admission days after the hostel fee is paid online, with a signed biodata form, the JEE (Advanced) welcome letter and declarations; mess registration and biometric/face registration are done at the same time.

sources.title: Instructions for Hostel Allotment and Mess Registration for First-year B.Tech/DD/BS Students (2026 batch)
Hostel Life

items.q: Do I get a tuition fee waiver at IIT Madras, and what do I actually pay in the first semester?
items.a: Tuition is Rs 1,00,000 per semester for the 2026-27 UG batch. SC/ST/PwD Indian students pay no tuition; General/OBC-NCL/EWS students with family income below Rs 1 lakh get full remission and those between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5 lakh get two-thirds off. With one-time fees (Rs 21,000), other semester charges and a Rs 5,000 caution deposit, the first-semester institute payment is Rs 1,41,402 (income above 5 lakh), Rs 74,735 (1-5 lakh) or Rs 41,402 (below 1 lakh, or SC/ST/PwD). Hostel fees are separate.

sources.title: Fees Circular for the New Students (UG & PG) of 2026 Batch - Annexure I, UG fee structure 2026-27

items.q: Is there a scholarship that covers the remaining one-third tuition for the Rs 1-5 lakh income group?
items.a: Yes. The institute's Merit-cum-Means scholarship goes to up to 25% of admitted UG students with parental income up to Rs 4.5 lakh a year who keep a GPA of 5.0 or more each semester; it exempts 67% of tuition. In February 2024 IIT Madras said MCM plus the government's two-thirds remission covered the full tuition of every eligible B.Tech/Dual Degree student in 2022-23 (490 students) and 2023-24 (495). SC/ST students under the income limit also get free messing and a Rs 250 monthly allowance.

items.q: How much are hostel and mess charges, and how does the mess work?
items.a: The July-November 2025 circular lists Rs 20,750 in mandatory hostel fees per semester for a new UG entrant: Rs 500 admission, Rs 8,000 Establishment-A, Rs 1,500 Establishment-B, Rs 500 RO water, Rs 250 waste disposal, Rs 5,000 utilities and a Rs 5,000 refundable deposit, plus an optional Rs 7,500 for Saarang, Shaastra and E-Summit. Advance mess charges are fixed after each mess tender and billed from registration. There are three messes (Himalaya, Nilgiri, Vindhya) with veg and non-veg options.

items.q: What comes with the hostel room, and do I need to bring a laptop?
items.a: Freshers' rooms come with a cot, chair, table, LAN port, fan and light; you must bring your own mattress, pillow, bedsheets, bucket, mug and a lock. The Council of Wardens publishes a hostel LAN manual, so a laptop is practical, but the 2026 allotment instructions do not list one as compulsory. Top-ranked SC/ST students under central government schemes get a one-time Rs 45,000 personal-computer grant (see the scholarships page). Parents cannot stay in the hostel during admission.

items.q: Is there a compulsory internship semester in the B.Tech programme?
items.a: Not for regular B.Tech programmes. The 5-year Engineering Design dual degree is the exception: it builds in a semester-long industry internship (the Design Project in Industry, usually in the 8th semester). Other students take summer internships arranged through the Placement and Internship Office, and good internships can turn into pre-placement offers: in the 2026-27 cycle a closed PPO must be issued by September 12 and accepted within 72 hours, while open PPOs may be issued until November 30.

sources.title: Engineering Design - Dual Degree Programme

items.q: Is there a CGPA cutoff to sit for campus placements?
items.a: The Placement and Internship Office does not publish a CGPA cutoff. Any student expected to graduate by the end of the academic year (2026-27 in the current cycle) can register in August for one year on paying Rs 500 (including GST), but students with four or more backlog courses cannot register. Each student may accept only one job offer and leaves the process once selected; if several offers arrive on the same day the student has 24 hours to choose. Interviews start on December 1.

items.q: Where exactly is the IIT Madras campus, and how do I reach it from the airport or railway station?
items.a: The campus is roughly 250 hectares of wooded land inside Chennai; the main (Adyar) gate is on Sardar Patel Road with Adyar and Velachery on either side, and there is also a Velachery gate. Chennai International Airport is about 15 km away (30-45 minutes by taxi), Chennai Central about 13 km and Egmore about 10 km; Guindy is the nearest metro station and city buses 5C, 21G, 21L, 23C, 47A and 49C serve the campus. Postal address: IIT P.O., Chennai 600 036.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction?
items.a: English. The B.Tech regulations state that instruction, examinations and project reports are all in English (R.2.8), so a comfortable working command of English is expected from day one.

sources.title: B.Tech / B.Tech (Honours) Ordinances and Regulations (2015 batch onwards), R.2.8

items.q: What dual-degree and interdisciplinary dual-degree (IDDD) options exist?
items.a: The B.Tech + M.Tech dual degree runs 10 semesters and is allotted directly through JoSAA in select branches; you pay B.Tech fees for the first 8 semesters. B.Tech students with CGPA 8.5 or higher after the 3rd semester and no U/W grades can opt for the Honours track during the 4th semester. IDDDs (12 as of December 2022, e.g. AI/ML, data science, robotics, electric vehicles, quantitative finance) are open to UG students of all engineering branches and typically start around the 6th semester.

items.q: Which newer or unusual programmes should I know about?
items.a: Three stand out. A B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics from the Wadhwani School of Data Science and AI started in 2024-25 with 50 seats, filled through JEE (Advanced) and JoSAA. The online BS in Data Science and Applications needs no JEE score, has no age limit, and lets learners exit at foundation, diploma, BSc or BS level, with fee waivers of up to 75% for family income under Rs 5 lakh. A BS in Electronic Systems was added in 2023.

items.q: Can I spend a semester abroad during my B.Tech?
items.a: Yes, through the Office of Global Engagement's semester exchange. UG, PG and dual-degree students who have finished at least three to four semesters with no backlogs can be nominated; a CGPA of 7.5 or higher is preferred when several students compete. Exchanges last five to six months, you may apply to only one partner university at a time, and the office estimates Rs 4-6 lakh per semester in costs depending on the country. Credit transfer is settled with the Academic Courses office.

sources.title: Semester Exchange - Office of Global Engagement

items.q: What academic minimums must I maintain to stay on track?
items.a: The B.Tech rules set a minimum CGPA of 5.0 over successfully completed courses at the end of each semester (R.10.3). An 'n minus 4' rule applies: to register for the 5th semester you must have cleared every 1st-semester course, and so on (R.6.5), which also applies to the 10-semester dual degree. Students with no backlog and a CGPA of 7.0 or above may take extra courses from the 4th semester onwards (R.6.4).

sources.title: B.Tech / B.Tech (Honours) Ordinances and Regulations (2015 batch onwards), R.6.4, R.6.5, R.10.3

items.q: How do I get around inside the campus, and what facilities are there?
items.a: The campus is fully residential and large enough to need its own transport: four buses and ten battery-powered vehicles run between the main zones every 20-30 minutes. There is an institute hospital with visiting specialists, X-ray and ambulance, SBI and Canara Bank branches with ATMs, two shopping complexes (one at the Student Facility Centre near Narmada hostel), a post office and several canteens open till late. The grounds are shared with blackbuck and spotted deer.

profile.about: NIT Tiruchirappalli began in 1964 as Regional Engineering College Tiruchirappalli, a joint venture of the central and Tamil Nadu governments, became an NIT with deemed-university status in 2003 and an Institution of National Importance in 2007. It is consistently the top-ranked NIT in NIRF, placing 9th in Engineering and 30th Overall in 2025. The 800-acre campus at Thuvakudi houses 17 departments, nine B.Tech programmes plus B.Arch, and roughly 7,500 students across UG, PG and doctoral levels, with a strong core-engineering tradition alongside its large CSE and ECE cohorts.

location.connectivityNote: The campus is at Thuvakudi on the Trichy-Thanjavur highway (NH 83) beside the BHEL township, about 17-22 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction and the central bus stand per the institute's own page; Thanjavur-bound buses take roughly 30 minutes. Trichy is a major Southern Railway junction and has an international airport with domestic and Gulf/Sri Lanka flights.

curriculumHighlights.text: B.Tech Regulations 2024 set a 160-credit (plus 3) degree over 58 courses: 56 credits of General Institute Requirements common to all branches, 52-55 credits of programme core, 36 credits of programme/open electives and 16 credits of essential laboratory work.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.2.2 credit distribution table

curriculumHighlights.text: An optional B.Tech (Honours) requires 15 extra credits from the department's honours basket starting in semester 5, with a minimum SGPA of 8.5 in every semester and at least a B grade in each honours course.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.3.0(5) and B.20.3 Honours eligibility

curriculumHighlights.text: A Minor is earned with 15 additional credits (at least five courses) from a single other department, available from semester 3; the minor certificate is issued separately alongside the degree.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.3.0(6) and B.20.4 Minor eligibility

curriculumHighlights.text: A compulsory summer internship or industrial training of at least six weeks after semester 6 carries 2 credits, assessed through a report and viva; final-year project work may also be done through Training & Placement internships or outside the institute.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.8.6 Internship / Industrial Training Evaluation

curriculumHighlights.text: Students can spend semester 7 or 8 at an approved foreign or Indian institution under exchange, study-abroad or academic-attachment programmes, provided courses already completed at NITT are not repeated.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.8.7 Study Abroad / Exchange Program

curriculumHighlights.text: NEP-style exit option: a student may leave after three years with a B.Sc. in the engineering discipline and return within the 12-semester maximum duration to finish the B.Tech.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.2.12 Exit and Re-Entry Provision

curriculumHighlights.text: Online (NPTEL/SWAYAM-type) courses of at least 12 weeks and short microcredit courses can be counted for credit; a student may register up to 28 credits a semester excluding honours, minor and online courses, and up to 25% of a course can be delivered by industry experts.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations 2024, B.2.11 industry experts, B.4.0(c) credit cap, online courses

summary.text: Campus life at NIT Trichy revolves around a large residential campus where nearly all students live in hostels. Student activity is organised under the Dean (Students' Welfare) into technical, cultural and social clubs, each with a faculty advisor, and the calendar is anchored by three student-run flagship events: Pragyan (techno-managerial fest, started 2005), Festember (cultural fest, started 1975, held in September) and NITTFEST, the inter-departmental cultural competition. Every department also runs its own two-day technical symposium, and the year in sports closes with Sportsfete. Facilities include a sports centre, a 400 m outdoor stadium and a 25 m pool.

items.q: How do I get a B.Tech seat at NIT Trichy?
items.a: Through JEE (Main) followed by JoSAA counselling; leftover seats are filled by CSAB special rounds. Your Class 12 marks matter for eligibility, but the seat itself is decided by your JEE Main rank and category. Foreign nationals, PIOs and NRIs come in through DASA instead. There is no separate NIT Trichy entrance test for B.Tech or B.Arch.

sources.title: NIT Trichy - Admission Procedure
NITT at a Glance

items.q: Which undergraduate branches does NIT Trichy offer?
items.a: Nine four-year B.Tech programmes: Chemical, Civil, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Electronics, Electronics and Communication, Instrumentation and Control, Mechanical, Metallurgical and Materials, and Production Engineering. There is also a five-year B.Arch and a four-year B.Sc. B.Ed. (admitted via NCET, not JoSAA). The JoSAA seat list carries only the 4-year B.Tech and 5-year B.Arch options; NIT Trichy does not offer B.Tech+M.Tech dual degrees through JoSAA.

sources.title: NIT Trichy - Academic Programmes
NITT at a Glance

items.q: Can I change my branch after first year?
items.a: Do not count on it. The B.Tech Regulations 2024 published on the institute site contain no branch-change (change of discipline) clause, so the branch allotted through JoSAA is effectively the one you graduate in. What the regulations do offer is a Minor (15 extra credits from one other department, starting in semester 3) and an Honours in your own branch, which is the institute's route to depth outside your allotted programme.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations (applicable from 2024 batch onwards)

items.q: Where exactly is the campus and how do I reach it?
items.a: The 800-acre campus sits on the Trichy-Thanjavur highway (NH 83, Tanjore Main Road) between the BHEL township and Thuvakudi, about 22 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction and the Central Bus Stand. The institute recommends taking any city bus from the junction to the central bus stand and then a Thanjavur-bound bus, roughly a 30-minute ride; taxis and autos also run from the city. Trichy has its own international airport and is a major Southern Railway junction with trains from Chennai, Bengaluru, Madurai and Coimbatore.

items.q: Where do first-year students stay, and what are the hostel rules for freshers?
items.a: First-year UG students are housed in separate, fenced first-year hostels (the hostels page lists Agate, Diamond and Coral as first-year boys' hostels); seniors may not enter them and freshers may not visit senior hostels. The 2026-27 rule book sets a 9:00 PM entry deadline for first-year hostels with roll call 9:00-9:30 PM on weekdays (9:30-10:00 PM on weekends) and fines for late entry. Good attendance in first year earns preference in second-year room allotment. Rooms are shared in first year; single rooms exist mainly in senior hostels such as Ruby, Emerald and Pearl.

sources.title: Hostel Rules & Regulations for Hostel Residents 2026-27
NIT Trichy - Hostels

items.q: What is the hostel fee for a newly admitted UG student?
items.a: For the odd semester 2026-27 a newly admitted UG (B.Tech/B.Arch/B.Sc.B.Ed.) student pays Rs 59,950 to the hostel account: Rs 3,600 admission fee, Rs 4,000 refundable caution deposit, Rs 10,650 establishment fee, Rs 17,700 rent/electricity/water/service charges and a Rs 24,000 mess advance covering five months. Payment is only through SBI Collect, and the receipt plus the hostel application form (with two Rs 100 stamp papers) are needed at hostel admission.

sources.title: Hostel Fees for Odd Semester 2026-27 (UG newly admitted students)

items.q: How much is the institute fee for the 2026 B.Tech batch?
items.a: Tuition is Rs 62,500 per semester for Open, EWS and OBC-NCL students. On top of that there is an annual fee paid in odd semesters (Rs 27,750 in year 1, rising to Rs 36,800 in year 4) and a one-time fee of Rs 35,300 that includes refundable institute and library deposits. So the first semester bill is Rs 1,25,550, the second semester Rs 62,500. SC, ST and PwD students pay no tuition, making their first semester Rs 63,050.

sources.title: Institute Fees Structure for 2026 Admission Batch - B.Tech.

items.q: Is there a tuition fee waiver based on family income?
items.a: Yes. Open, EWS and OBC-NCL students with family income below Rs 1 lakh a year get full remission of the Rs 62,500 tuition; those with income between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5 lakh get two-thirds off (Rs 41,667). SC/ST/PwD students are exempt from tuition regardless of income. You must submit a parental income certificate for the previous financial year and file the income-based Tuition Fee Remission form available on the Fees Section page, which also posts the annual remission notice for the newly admitted batch.

sources.title: Institute Fees Structure for 2026 Admission Batch - B.Tech.
NIT Trichy - Fees Section

items.q: What is the medium of instruction?
items.a: English. The B.Tech regulations state that instruction, examinations and project reports are all in English. Exchange or study-abroad semesters are also allowed only at institutions that teach in English.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations (applicable from 2024 batch onwards)

items.q: Is there a compulsory internship in the B.Tech programme?
items.a: Yes. Every B.Tech student must complete an internship or industrial training of at least six weeks in the summer after the 6th semester. It is registered along with 7th-semester courses, carries 2 credits and is graded on a report plus a viva conducted by the HoD and programme coordinator. Internships arranged through the Training and Placement office can also be turned into the final-year project with departmental approval.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations (applicable from 2024 batch onwards)

items.q: What are the Honours, Minor and early-exit options?
items.a: Honours: earn 15 extra credits from your own department's honours basket from semester 5 onward, keep an SGPA of at least 8.5 in every semester and at least a B in each honours course to graduate with B.Tech (Honours). Minor: 15 extra credits from a single other department starting semester 3, certified separately alongside the degree. Exit option: a student may leave after three years with a B.Sc. in the engineering discipline and return within the 12-semester limit to finish the B.Tech.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations (applicable from 2024 batch onwards)

items.q: Is there a CGPA cutoff for campus placements?
items.a: The institute itself does not set a CGPA bar; each recruiter fixes its own eligibility (branches, academic cutoff, degree level), and the T&P office negotiates to widen the pool. NIT Trichy follows a one-job policy so that offers spread across branches, and students who plan higher studies, GATE/PSU or UPSC may opt out of the placement preparation series. Everyone who wants placements must take part in that series. For reference, the T&P page reports 80.4% of registered UG students placed in 2025-26 (CSE 88.1%, ECE 85.5%), down from 86.2% in 2024-25.

items.q: What are the rules on laptops, appliances, vehicles and mess in the hostels?
items.a: Laptops and phones are allowed but are your own responsibility: keep them locked away and lock the room when you step out. Immersion heaters, kettles, irons, air coolers, personal Wi-Fi extenders and routers are banned in rooms, private cooking is prohibited, and powered vehicles (bikes, scooters) are not permitted for students on campus; cycles are fine. Food is served in 13 messes with South Indian, North Indian, Andhra, Kerala and mixed menus, including dedicated first-year messes; taking food or utensils out of the mess is not allowed.

NIT Trichy - Messes

items.q: How strict are attendance and degree requirements?
items.a: A B.Tech needs 160-163 credits over eight semesters, and you cannot take more than twelve semesters in total. At least 75% attendance is required in every course to sit the final assessment, and first-year students must also complete NCC, NSO or NSS (45 hours a semester) within the first four semesters. First class with distinction goes to those finishing in eight semesters with CGPA 8.5 or above and no failed courses; first class needs CGPA 6.5 or more.

sources.title: B.Tech. Regulations (applicable from 2024 batch onwards)

items.q: What happens after I get a JoSAA allotment: when do I report and when do classes start?
items.a: For the 2026-27 batch the institute ran online reporting on 15-17 August 2026 (no campus visit needed for this step), followed by physical reporting department-wise at Barn Hall in the Administrative Block on 18-20 August, an orientation programme on 21-25 August and the start of classes on 27 August 2026. The B.Tech admissions page carries the registration link, balance-fee payment details and the list of documents to upload, so keep checking it after your allotment.

profile.about: NIT Warangal began in 1959 as the first of the Regional Engineering Colleges, with its foundation stone laid by Jawaharlal Nehru, and is today an Institute of National Importance funded by the Ministry of Education. It is a fully residential campus of about 250 acres with roughly 7,000 students and 400 faculty across 13 academic departments, offering B.Tech in ten specialisations alongside dual-degree, integrated M.Sc., M.Tech, MBA and PhD programmes. Its reputation rests on strong core-engineering departments, a large doctoral programme, an active sponsored-research and consultancy portfolio, and a consistent place among the top 25–30 engineering institutes in NIRF.

curriculumHighlights.text: There is no branch change at the end of the first year: the 2024-25 UG regulations state this explicitly, so the JoSAA/CSAB allotment is the branch a student graduates in.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - rule 2.8 (no branch change)

curriculumHighlights.text: The B.Tech needs a minimum of 150-160 credits (as fixed by each department) with a CGPA of at least 5.00, plus mandatory non-credit courses; the degree takes at least four years and must be completed within eight. One lecture hour a week over a 14-week semester earns one credit, a lab hour half a credit.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - rules 3.4-3.5 (credits, degree requirements)

curriculumHighlights.text: Minor programmes: 15 extra credits (five courses, or four plus a project) in a discipline offered by another department, from the 3rd semester, for a one-time fee. A student may take one minor, two minors, or a minor plus honours; an NCC minor with relaxed CGPA eligibility is open to school-level NCC cadets.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - section 16 (Minor Program)

curriculumHighlights.text: Honours: 15 additional credits within the student's own department from the 5th semester, finishing by the 8th; the degree is awarded as the discipline 'with Honors'. Honours credits can be carried into an M.Tech in the relevant specialisation at the institute.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - section 17 (Honors Program) and M.Tech credit transfer note

curriculumHighlights.text: Every student must complete either a 6-8 week summer internship (industry, research organisation or a premier academic institute, NIT Warangal included) or an EPICS community-service project under a faculty guide, and present the work to a departmental evaluation committee.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - rule 9.8 (Summer/research internship / EPICS)

curriculumHighlights.text: An optional 8th-semester internship arranged through the placement centre (CCPD) is open to students with CGPA above 6.50 and no backlogs up to the 7th semester; the remaining 8th-semester courses are done by self-study or SWAYAM/NPTEL, and the internship project counts as the final-year project.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - section 18 (Semester Internship)

curriculumHighlights.text: The curriculum mixes basic-science, engineering-science and humanities cores with programme-core and elective courses, open electives (sciences, engineering, humanities or management), minor/major projects and mandatory non-credit courses. Students below 5.00 CGPA after the 2nd semester are flagged via the ERP.

sources.title: Academic Regulations of UG Programs 2024-25 - section 3.1 (course structure) and rule 9.9 (slow learners)

research.note: NIT Warangal runs a large doctoral programme for an NIT: its NIRF 2025 submission lists 642 full-time and 433 part-time PhD scholars enrolled up to 2023-24, with 125 PhDs (101 full-time, 24 part-time) awarded in 2023-24 alone. Externally funded work in FY 2023-24 comprised 161 sponsored projects from 39 agencies worth about Rs 19.4 crore, plus 107 consultancy projects for 84 client organisations worth about Rs 2.9 crore. The institute also hosts a Centre of Excellence in Additive Manufacturing and a Centre for Teaching and Learning.

summary.text: Campus life at NIT Warangal is coordinated by the Dean (Student Welfare) through the Student Activity Centre, which organises activity under three umbrella bodies on the Student Council: the Technical, Cultural, and Film & Music Societies, each running specialised clubs from robotics and ham radio to debating, photography, and dance-drama. The Centre for Sports Activities maintains a full stadium complex and runs freshers' tournaments feeding into the annual Inter-NIT Sports Meet. The calendar's two flagship festivals are Technozion, a technical fest held every October since 2006, and Spring Spree, a cultural fest tracing back to 1978 and held every February.

items.q: When was NIT Warangal founded and what is its institutional status?
items.a: The institute opened in 1959 as one of the country's first Regional Engineering Colleges, a joint venture of the central government and the state of Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana). It was renamed National Institute of Technology in 2002 and, in 2007, Parliament declared it an Institute of National Importance, putting it on the same statutory footing as the other NITs and funded directly by the Ministry of Education.

sources.title: NIT Warangal Communication Handbook 2024 - A Brief Introduction (foundation 10 Oct 1959)

items.q: Where is the NIT Warangal campus and how large is it?
items.a: The residential campus sits just outside Kazipet on the Hyderabad-Warangal highway (NH-202), in Hanamkonda, Telangana, and spreads across roughly 250 acres. Most students reach it by train to Kazipet Junction, which many long-distance trains serve directly, or to Warangal railway station a little further away; the nearest commercial airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, about a two-and-a-half-hour drive.

items.q: How do I get admission into the B.Tech program at NIT Warangal?
items.a: Admission to the B.Tech, dual-degree (B.Tech + M.Tech) and five-year Integrated M.Sc. programmes runs on a candidate's JEE Main rank, with seats allotted through the JoSAA counselling rounds; any seats still open afterwards are filled through CSAB's special rounds, again by JEE Main rank.

items.q: Is there a way into NIT Warangal besides the regular JoSAA counselling?
items.a: Yes. Foreign nationals, NRIs and PIOs can enter B.Tech through separate schemes -- DASA, Study in India, ICCR sponsorship and the Nepal COMPEX quota -- each with its own eligibility and fee slab listed on the admissions site. The institute also runs a four-year B.Sc. B.Ed. under the national Integrated Teacher Education Programme as a standalone admission stream outside JoSAA.

items.q: Can I switch branches after joining NIT Warangal?
items.a: No. Under the 2024-25 undergraduate regulations there is no provision to change branch after the first year, so the programme a student is allotted through JoSAA or CSAB is the one the degree is awarded in.

items.q: Where does NIT Warangal stand in the NIRF rankings?
items.a: In the government's 2025 NIRF list, NIT Warangal was placed 28th among engineering institutes and 63rd in the overall category, a step down from 21st (engineering) and 53rd (overall) in both 2023 and 2024, though it has stayed inside the top 30 engineering institutes every year since the category was tracked here.

items.q: What undergraduate branches and programmes does NIT Warangal offer?
items.a: Across its 14 academic departments, B.Tech is offered in Civil, Electrical and Electronics (plus an Electric Mobility variant), Mechanical, Electronics and Communication (plus VLSI Design and Technology), Metallurgical and Materials, Chemical, Computer Science (plus an Artificial Intelligence and Data Science variant), Biotechnology and Mathematics and Computing engineering. The Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry departments each run a five-year Integrated M.Sc., and the Mathematics department also coordinates a four-year ITEP B.Sc. B.Ed.

items.q: How many students and faculty does NIT Warangal have?
items.a: The institute's own 2024 handbook puts total enrolment at roughly 7,000 students, while its NIRF 2025 submission lists 398 faculty members as of 2023-24 -- a comfortable core-engineering faculty base for a single-campus NIT of this size.

items.q: Does NIT Warangal offer dual-degree or integrated master's options alongside the four-year B.Tech?
items.a: Yes. Students can enter directly through JoSAA into a five-year B.Tech + M.Tech dual degree in Metallurgical and Materials Engineering or in Chemical Engineering, and separately into a five-year Integrated M.Sc. in Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry -- all allotted the same way as the four-year B.Tech, by JEE Main rank.

items.q: How research-active is NIT Warangal at the doctoral level?
items.a: It runs an unusually large PhD programme for an NIT: its own NIRF 2025 submission reports 1,075 scholars enrolled (642 full-time, 433 part-time) as of 2023-24, with 125 doctorates awarded that year, alongside 161 externally sponsored research projects and 107 consultancy assignments in the same period. The institute also houses dedicated centres for additive manufacturing and for teaching and learning.

items.q: Who are some well-known people who studied at NIT Warangal?
items.a: Its alumni span several fields: Pushmeet Kohli leads research at Google DeepMind, Sudhir Kumar Mishra heads DRDO and the BrahMos missile programme, Sujatha Gidla is a published author, and Shreya Dhanwanthary and Kartikeya Gummakonda are known from Hindi and Telugu film and streaming work. Others have gone into Parliament, the civil services and academic leadership at other institutes.
